title: r/beyondthebump
tagline: New parents asking each other what's actually worth buying.
audience: Parents of babies and toddlers, exhausted and practical. They ask for recommendations constantly and trust other parents far more than advertising.
overview:
A support community for the first years of parenthood. Product questions come up continuously — what's worth the money, what was a waste, what actually solved a problem at 3am.

The recommendations that carry weight here come from other parents, which means the route in is being a parent who happens to make something, not a brand.
discussions:
What baby gear was worth it and what wasn't
Sleep, feeding and routine questions
Gift recommendations for new parents
Milestone and photo ideas
Hand-me-down and secondhand advice
loves:
Honest assessments including what didn't work
Practical products that solve a real daily problem
Parents speaking from actual experience
dislikes:
Marketing dressed as a recommendation
Judgement about parenting choices
Expensive products pushed at exhausted people
rules:
Self-promotion is not permitted
Undisclosed brand accounts are banned
Judgement-free rules are enforced strictly
approach: Participate as a parent, never as a shop. What you learn about which gifts new parents actually value — and which ones get quietly re-gifted — should shape what you make.
tags: baby, parenting, newborn, nursery, gift, blanket, clothes

title: #nurseryinspo
tagline: Expectant parents building a room, with months of lead time and a budget.
audience: Parents-to-be designing a nursery. They're planning for a fixed deadline with a clear budget, and they buy decor, signs, blankets and prints in one concentrated burst.
overview:
One of the most reliable buying moments in retail: someone furnishing a room by a known date, emotionally invested, browsing for months beforehand.

The aesthetic is consistent — neutrals, natural materials, soft textures — and products that fit it get saved into boards and bought weeks later.
discussions:
Nursery reveals and room tours
Shelf styling and wall arrangements
Colour palettes, overwhelmingly neutral
Small-space and shared-room solutions
Personalised decor with the baby's name
loves:
Products styled into a complete nursery rather than shot alone
Neutral, timeless palettes that photograph softly
Personalisation, which dominates this category
dislikes:
Bright primary-colour plastic, against the prevailing taste
Products shot out of context
Unsafe items near a cot in styled photos
rules:
Safe-sleep guidance matters — styled cots full of blankets attract criticism
Algorithmic relevance applies to tagging
Paid partnerships require disclosure
approach: Shoot everything styled into a nursery corner, in neutrals, and lead with personalisation. Parents here are planning months ahead — being saved now is what converts later.
tags: nursery, baby, decor, sign, blanket, print, name

title: r/Mommit
tagline: A large parenting community where gift recommendations circulate constantly.
audience: Mothers across all stages of parenting. Enormous, chatty, and full of gift-recommendation threads for birthdays, showers and holidays.
overview:
A general parenting community with a strong social element. Alongside the support conversations, product and gift threads run continuously — baby shower gifts, first birthday ideas, what to buy a friend who just had a baby.

Those threads are pure demand signal, and the answers come from parents naming things they genuinely loved.
discussions:
Gift ideas for showers, births and first birthdays
What products were genuinely worth buying
Milestone photo and keepsake ideas
Hand-me-down and reuse conversations
General parenting support
loves:
Keepsake items that get kept rather than outgrown
Personalised gifts, consistently top-recommended
Realistic price points
dislikes:
Brand accounts participating
Products that are clearly impractical for actual babies
Overpriced items pushed as essentials
rules:
Self-promotion is not allowed
Undisclosed marketing is banned and actively watched for
Support-first culture is enforced
approach: Read the gift threads rather than posting in them. What parents repeatedly name as the gifts they kept — usually personalised keepsakes — is exactly what you should be making.
tags: baby, parenting, gift, keepsake, blanket, personalised, nursery

title: Pinterest: baby showers & nurseries
tagline: Planning starts months out, and Pinterest is where it happens.
audience: Expectant parents and shower hosts planning against a fixed date. Long lead times, high intent, and saves that persist for months before converting.
overview:
Baby is one of Pinterest's strongest categories precisely because it's deadline-driven planning. Someone pinning nursery ideas in March is buying in June, and your pin stays in their board the entire time.

Gift-idea searches are especially valuable — the person searching is buying for someone else and has no strong preference yet.
discussions:
Baby shower themes, decor and favours
Nursery mood boards by colour and style
Gift-idea roundups for showers and births
Milestone photo setups
Keepsake and memory-book ideas
loves:
Vertical images with clear text overlay describing the item
Keyword-rich descriptions matching how planners search
Seasonal and occasion-specific pins
dislikes:
Square social crops that perform poorly in a vertical feed
Pins with dead or misleading links
One pin per product, which catches only one search
rules:
It's a search engine — keywords determine discoverability
Shopping features need a claimed account and working links
Seasonal indexing runs well ahead of the occasion
approach: Make several vertical pins per product targeting different searches — "baby shower gift", "personalised nursery decor", "newborn keepsake". Pins compound; what you post now sells for years.
tags: baby, nursery, shower, gift, keepsake, decor, personalised
